interval-circuit-timer: Tap Tabata, HIIT, Circuit, Every minute, Boxing rounds or Study sprints, or start from the default numbers.
Change the seconds of work and rest, the number of rounds and sets, the rest between sets and the get ready time. Add a name for each round if you like.
Keep the beep for the last three seconds and at each change, and the big countdown, or switch them off.
Tap Start timer. Green shows work and blue shows rest. Use the arrow keys, space bar or the buttons to skip, pause or close.
exam-hall-display: Choose a ready length such as a three-hour exam, class test, short test or quick quiz, or type your own minutes and warning time.
Write the exam name, the subject or class and the rules students must see, one per line.
Start when you press the button, or at a set time, in which case the screen counts down to the start.
Tap Start the exam screen. It shows the clock, the time left and the rules. It turns amber for the last minutes and red with "Pens down" at the end.
menu-board-display: Pick a sample or start empty
Start from a cafe menu, daily specials or a price list, then replace the names and prices with your own, or paste many lines at once.
Each item has a name, a price, an optional note and an optional section such as Hot drinks or Snacks.
Set how many items show on each screen, how many seconds each screen stays, a rupee or other symbol before prices and a screen colour.
Open the page on the TV, tap Show on screen and leave it. It loops through the sections and pages until you close it.
queue-token-display: Set the heading and number style
Type a heading such as Counter 2 or the doctor’s room, an optional letter before the number and how many digits to show.
Press Call next number as each person is called. Go back one if you pressed too soon, or jump to any number.
Tap Show on the big screen. It shows the current number in huge digits, the next three numbers and the ones called earlier.
On the big screen use the Next button, the right arrow or the space bar to call the next number. The count is saved on the device, so it survives a reload.
daily-timings-board: Start from Temple or prayer hall, Clinic or office hours, Community hall, or Event programme, or add your own times.
Each row has a time, what happens and an optional note such as the room. You can enter them in any order, because the board sorts them.
Show times as 12-hour or 24-hour, show or hide the clock, and choose a light or dark screen.
Tap Show on screen. The activity that is on now turns green, the next one is marked, and earlier ones fade.
spelling-bee-display: Start from Animals, School words or Tricky spellings, or add your own words with a meaning or clue. You can also paste a list at once.
Spell it shows the clue first and then reveals the word with its letters. Read it shows the word first and then reveals the meaning.
Click to reveal and move on, or tick Move on by itself and set the seconds to think and the seconds to show the answer. Shuffle the words if you like.
Tap Start the bee. Click, press space or the right arrow to reveal and move on; the left arrow goes back.
notice-board-display: Start from Welcome board, Birthdays and wishes or Notices, or add your own messages one by one.
Each message has a heading, an optional line or two of text, a colour and an optional picture.
Choose how many seconds each message stays on the screen.
Tap Show on screen. The messages loop full screen until you close it.
step-by-step-routine-display: Pick a ready routine or start empty
Start from Morning stretch, Desk break, Cool-down stretch, Breathing and relaxing, Kids’ morning routine or Classroom stations, or build your own from scratch.
Add steps with pictures or your own
Add a stretch or exercise from the picture list, or add your own step such as "Add the flour" or "Station 2". Each step has a name, an optional cue, seconds and an optional picture of your own.
Choose the get ready time, the soft beep, the big countdown, a light or dark screen and an optional logo in the corner.
Tap Start routine. Each step shows its name, cue, picture, countdown and the next step. Use the arrow keys, space bar or buttons to go back, pause or close.

screensIntervalTimer.title: Interval and Circuit Timer
screensIntervalTimer.subtitle: A free full-screen interval timer for work and rest rounds, sets and named exercises. Tabata, HIIT, circuit, EMOM, boxing and study sprints, with beeps.
faq: What is the difference between Tabata, HIIT and a circuit?

They are all ways of splitting time into work and rest. Tabata is 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest for 8 rounds. HIIT usually uses longer work periods, for example 40 seconds of work and 20 seconds of rest. A circuit moves through a list of exercises, one per round, and then repeats. Pick a ready timer and change the numbers to suit your group.
Can I name each round?

Yes. Type one exercise name per line in the names box and the timer shows each name in turn, repeating the list when it reaches the end. The next name also shows at the bottom so people can get ready.
Can I use it for something other than exercise?
Yes. Study sprints of 25 minutes with a 5 minute break, cooking steps, speaking practice, boxing rounds, music practice and classroom activities all use the same work and rest pattern.
Does it work on a gym TV, a projector or a phone?

Yes. Open the page on the device connected to the screen and tap Start timer. It goes fullscreen where the browser allows it, tries to keep the screen awake and uses very large numbers so they can be read from across a room. The beeps need the volume on. You can add your gym logo to the corner of the screen.
Why is the screen green and blue?
Green means work and blue means rest, so people can tell what to do without reading the numbers. The countdown turns red in the last three seconds of work.
Is this medical advice? Is the timer right for me?

No. This is general information and not medical advice. Choose work and rest times that suit your level, warm up first, and stop if you feel pain, dizziness or chest discomfort. If you have a health condition or have not exercised for a long time, talk to a doctor or a qualified trainer first.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensExamHall.title: Exam Hall Display
screensExamHall.subtitle: A free full-screen exam timer for a hall or classroom with a big clock, time left, start and end times, rules and a last-minutes warning. Works on any screen.
faq: How do I use it in an exam hall?

Open the page on the computer connected to the projector or TV, choose the length and rules, and tap Start the exam screen. Students see the current time, the time left, when the exam started and ends, and the rules. You can start it with a button or at a set time. You can add your school or centre logo to the corner of the screen.
What happens near the end?

For the last minutes you choose (for example 15), the screen turns amber and says how many minutes remain. When time is up it turns red and shows "Pens down". An optional beep marks the start, the warning and the end.
Can I show the instructions to students?
Yes. Type one rule per line, for example write your roll number first, no mobile phones, raise your hand for help. They show under the clock for the whole exam.
Which exams is it for?
School and college tests, board exam practice, entrance exam mock tests, tuition and coaching centre tests, driving or skill tests, and any timed assessment where a room needs one shared clock.
Can I start it at a fixed time such as 10:00 AM?
Yes. Choose Start at a set time and enter the time. Until then the screen counts down to the start. The page follows the clock of the device, so check it against the hall clock before you begin.
Is there a quiz version with questions?
Yes. The Classroom Quiz Display shows questions, options, answers and explanations in learn, mock exam and real exam modes with a timer on each question.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensMenuBoard.title: Menu and Price Board Display
screensMenuBoard.subtitle: A free digital menu board for a cafe, restaurant, salon or shop. Add items with prices, group them in sections and loop them full screen on any TV or monitor.
faq: How do I put my menu on a TV?
Connect a computer, phone or smart TV browser to the screen, open this page, add your items and tap Show on screen. The menu goes fullscreen and loops by itself, with several items on each screen.
Can I use it for something other than food?
Yes. Salons, laundries, repair shops, tuition centres, gyms and service businesses can show a price list. Leave the section empty and the board uses your heading.
Can I show today’s specials?
Yes. Start from the Daily specials sample, change the dishes and notes each morning, and show it on the counter screen. The page remembers your last list on that device.
Can I use my own currency?
Yes. Choose a symbol such as ₹, $, € or £ to put before prices that are only numbers, or choose no symbol and type prices exactly as you want them, for example "From 99" or "Ask us".
How many items can I show?
Up to 300 items. Choose 3 to 10 items on each screen so the text stays large enough to read from the queue, and the board moves through all of them.
Can I add pictures of dishes or my logo?

Yes. Each item can have its own small picture, shown beside its name and price, and you can add your shop logo to the corner of the screen. Pictures are shrunk in your browser and kept only on this device. You can use the board with no pictures at all.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensQueueToken.title: Queue Token Display
screensQueueToken.subtitle: A free now serving token display. Press Next to call the next number and show it huge on a screen, with a chime, counter name, letter prefix and recent numbers.
faq: How does the token display work?

Give people numbered slips or tell them their number. Press Next each time you call someone and the screen shows the new number in very large digits with a chime. The next three numbers show underneath so people know when their turn is close.
Where can I use it?

Clinics and doctors’ waiting rooms, pharmacies, bank and post office counters, government service desks, repair shops, salons, canteens, passport photo studios, temples and any place with a queue. You can add your clinic or shop logo to the corner of the screen.
Can I use letters and several counters?

Yes. Add a letter before the number, for example A, so tokens read A12, and set the heading to the counter or room. For several counters, open the page on each device and give each its own letter and heading.
Does it show on a second screen by itself?
No. Nothing is sent anywhere, so the screen that shows the number must be the device you control. Connect that device to the TV or monitor and use its keyboard or buttons to call numbers.
What if I press Next by mistake?
Use Go back one, or the left arrow on the big screen. You can also type the right number in Jump to number, or start again from 1 at the start of a new day.
Can I turn off the chime?
Yes. Untick the chime in the settings. A light screen is also available for bright rooms.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensTimingsBoard.title: Daily Timings Board
screensTimingsBoard.subtitle: A free digital timings board for a temple, clinic, hall, office or event. Add times and activities and the screen highlights what is on now and what is next.
faq: What is a timings board for?

It shows the day’s schedule on a screen and highlights what is on now and what is next. It suits a temple or prayer hall, a clinic or office with opening hours, a community hall or society with activities, and an event with a programme. You can add a logo to the corner, for example your temple, clinic or society.
Does it update by itself?
Yes. The board follows the clock of the device, so the activity that is on turns green and the next one is marked without anyone touching it. Earlier activities fade.
Do I have to enter the times in order?
No. The board sorts the rows by time for you. Rows without a valid time go to the end.
Can I show 24-hour or 12-hour times?
Yes. Choose 12-hour (2:30 PM) or 24-hour (14:30) in the settings.
Can I change the timings for different days?
Edit the rows before you show the board. The page keeps your last list on that device, so you only change what is different for the day.
Does it need the internet?
The board works from the page once it has loaded and uses the clock of your device. It does not look up any times, so check that the device clock is right.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensSpellingBee.title: Spelling and Vocabulary Bee Display
screensSpellingBee.subtitle: A free spelling bee and vocabulary game for the classroom screen. Add words with clues, show a clue and reveal the word or its meaning. Manual or automatic.
faq: How does the spelling bee work?

In Spell it, the screen shows a clue such as a meaning. Students write or say the spelling, then the teacher clicks to reveal the word, which is shown with its letters spaced out. In Read it, the word shows first and a click reveals its meaning or a sentence.
Can I use my own words?

Yes. Type each word with a meaning, clue or sentence, or paste a list with one word per line in the form word, clue. Ready lists for animals, school words and tricky spellings are included as examples.
Can it run by itself?
Yes. Tick Move on by itself, then set the seconds to think and the seconds to show the answer. Or leave it off and click to reveal, which gives you control of the pace.
Which classes is it for?
It works for primary and middle school spelling practice, vocabulary revision in any subject (science terms, maths words, new words in a language class), tuition classes and family spelling games.
Can I shuffle the words?
Yes. Tick Shuffle the words and the order changes every time you start. Your list itself is not changed.
Can I add pictures to the words?

Yes. Each word can have a picture clue, for example a photo of an animal or an object. In Spell it the picture shows with the clue, and the word is revealed under it. You can also add your school logo to the corner of the screen.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensNoticeBoard.title: Notice and Greeting Board Display
screensNoticeBoard.subtitle: A free digital notice board for an office, school, shop or home. Rotate welcome messages, birthday wishes, notices and reminders with colours and pictures.
faq: What can I show on it?

Welcome messages, birthday and anniversary wishes, notices, holiday closures, meeting reminders, thank-you messages, safety reminders and event announcements. Each message can have its own colour and a picture.
Where would I use it?
Office reception and break rooms, school entrances and staff rooms, shops, clinics, community halls, societies, hostels, events and family celebrations on a TV.
Can I add pictures and videos?

Yes. Each message can have a picture, such as a photo of the birthday person or a logo, or a short video that plays muted and loops during that message. You can also add a logo to the corner of the screen. Pictures are kept in your browser. A video comes from your device and is not uploaded, but it is not kept when you reload the page, so add it again next time.
Does it loop?
Yes. The messages play one after the other and start again from the first when they reach the end, until you close the screen.
How is this different from Display Studio?

Display Studio turns PDFs, Word files and pictures you already have into a slideshow. This tool is for typed messages with a heading, text, colour and optional picture, which you can change in a few seconds.
How many messages can I add?
Up to 300. A short loop of five to ten messages works best for a screen that people pass quickly.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

screensRoutineDisplay.title: Step-by-Step Routine Display
screensRoutineDisplay.subtitle: A free full-screen routine timer for any step-by-step activity. Stretches come with pictures; add your own steps, cues, pictures and times for anything else.
faq: What can I use it for?

Any activity that is a list of steps with a time on each: a stretch or yoga sequence, a warm-up or cool-down, a home exercise routine, a breathing or relaxation break, a classroom station rotation, a kids’ morning routine, recipe or cooking steps, a lab procedure, a workshop or shop checklist and a presentation practice run.
Does it have pictures?

Yes for stretches and exercises. The list has 182 exercises and stretches, 64 of them stretches, each with two pictures that fade into each other. These come from the free-exercise-db project, which is in the public domain. There are no yoga pose pictures, because we did not find a yoga picture set that is clearly free to use, but you can add your own picture to any step.
Can I add my own pictures to steps?
Yes. Every step can have a picture of your own, for example a photo of a pose, a diagram, a product or a step in a recipe. The picture is shrunk in your browser and shown above the step name.
Can I use it for yoga?

Yes. Type the pose names and cues, set the hold time and add your own pose photos or leave them out. The ready stretch sequences are a good start for gentle mobility work. For yoga classes the screen keeps the time and the teacher leads the pose.
Can I paste a list of steps?
Yes. Choose Paste many at once and put one step per line in the form name, cue, seconds. The cue and seconds are optional.
Is this medical advice?

No. For exercises and stretches this is general information and not medical advice. Move gently, never force a stretch, and stop if something hurts. If you are pregnant, injured, recovering or have a health condition, check with a doctor or a qualified teacher first.
Is my information uploaded or stored?
No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is saved on this device only. Nothing is sent to {{siteName}}. The page still loads advertising and other resources from the network.

sections.heading: A timer people can read from across the room
paragraphs: An interval timer splits a session into rounds of work and rest. This one fills the screen with a huge countdown, changes colour between work and rest, beeps in the last three seconds and shows the name of the next round, so a group can follow it without looking at a phone.
It suits a home workout on a laptop, a gym or studio TV, a school PT lesson on a classroom screen, a boxing club, or anyone who wants a clean timer without an account.

sections.heading: Ready timers for common formats
paragraphs: Tabata is 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest for 8 rounds, which takes 4 minutes. HIIT in this tool starts at 40 seconds of work and 20 seconds of rest for 10 rounds. A circuit gives each station its own name and repeats the list for a number of sets. Every minute on the minute gives you a new round at the start of each minute. Boxing rounds use 3 minutes of work and 1 minute of rest.
Every number can be changed, so you can turn any of them into your own format and the timer shows the total time before you start.

sections.heading: Beyond the gym
paragraphs: Teachers use work and rest rounds for station activities, spelling practice and quick group tasks. Students use 25 minute study sprints with 5 minute breaks. Musicians use them for practice blocks, and cooks for timed steps.
This page gives general information and not medical advice. Warm up, pick times that suit your level and stop if something hurts.

sections.heading: One clock for the whole room
paragraphs: In an exam hall everyone needs to see the same time. This display fills a projector or TV with the current time, the time left in very large digits and the time the exam ends, so invigilators do not have to announce the time again and again.
You can add the rules for the day, such as writing the roll number first or keeping phones away, so they stay in view for the whole exam.

sections.heading: Warnings that do not need an announcement
paragraphs: The screen changes colour for the last minutes of the exam and again when time is up, so students and invigilators notice without a shout. An optional beep marks the start, the beginning of the warning and the end.
The warning time is your choice. Fifteen minutes suits a long paper, five minutes suits a short test.

sections.heading: Good for tests of any size
paragraphs: Use it for a class test, a mock exam, a coaching centre test series, an interview round or an online examination room. Pair it with the Classroom Quiz Display when you want questions shown on the screen as well.
Check the device clock against the hall clock before you begin.

sections.heading: A digital menu board without the software
paragraphs: A menu screen by the counter helps customers decide before they reach the front of the queue. This page turns any TV or monitor with a browser into a menu board: type the items and prices, choose how many show at once and leave it running.
Items are grouped into sections such as hot drinks, cold drinks and snacks, with each section shown on its own screen and long sections split across pages.

sections.heading: Easy to keep up to date
paragraphs: Change a price, add today’s special or remove a sold-out dish in a moment, and the screen shows the new list the next time you start it. The page saves your list in the browser, so it is ready the next morning.
You can paste a whole list from a message or a document, with one item per line in the form name, price, note.

sections.heading: For cafes, shops and service businesses
paragraphs: Cafes and tea stalls, bakeries, tiffin services, salons, tailors, photo studios, repair shops, coaching classes and canteens can all use the same board. Pick a colour that matches your shop and leave the board looping all day.
Prices are shown exactly as you type them, so read them through once before you put the board on display.

sections.heading: A simple numbered queue
paragraphs: A token screen keeps a queue calm. People know their number and when it is called, and staff do not have to shout names across the room.

Press Next and the whole screen changes to the new number, with a chime to catch attention. The next three numbers and the numbers called before are shown, so someone who missed a call can see where the queue is.

sections.heading: Made for small businesses
paragraphs: You do not need a ticket machine or a subscription. Hand out numbered slips from a notebook, or just tell people their number, and run the display from a laptop, a tablet or a phone connected to a TV.
Clinics, pharmacies, document service centres, salons and workshops can each set their own heading, letter and digits.

sections.heading: Tips for a busy counter
paragraphs: Use big digits and a dark screen for a hall, and a light screen for a bright shop front. Start again from 1 each morning. If you work with two staff at one desk, agree who presses Next.
The count is saved in the browser, so a refresh does not lose your place.

sections.heading: What is on now, at a glance
paragraphs: People walk past a notice board and want one answer: what is happening now and what is next. This board follows the clock, turns the current activity green and marks the next one, so they do not have to read the whole list.
It sorts the times for you, so you can add a late change at the bottom without worrying about the order.

sections.heading: Places that use a timings board
paragraphs: Temples, gurdwaras, churches, mosques and prayer halls can show prayer and opening times. Clinics, shops and offices can show hours and breaks. Community halls, societies and clubs can show the day’s activities. Events and conferences can show the programme.
Samples for each are included. Replace the times with your own.

sections.heading: Keeping the board correct
paragraphs: The times are shown exactly as you type them. Check them once before the board goes on display, and update them when timings change for a festival, a holiday or a season.
The board uses the clock of the device it runs on, so make sure that clock is correct.

sections.heading: Spelling practice the whole class can see
paragraphs: A spelling bee is more fun when everyone can see the clue and the answer. This display shows a clue in large text, waits for the class to try, then reveals the word with its letters spread out so students can check their own spelling.
The other way round also works: show the word and reveal its meaning, which suits vocabulary lessons.

sections.heading: Easy word lists
paragraphs: Add words one by one or paste a list from a worksheet. Each word has a meaning, clue or sentence. Ready lists are included for younger classes, everyday school words and spellings that many people get wrong.
Your last list is saved on the device, so you can run it again with another class and shuffle the order.

sections.heading: Manual or automatic
paragraphs: In manual mode the teacher clicks to reveal and move on, which is best when students answer aloud or on paper. In automatic mode the screen waits for the thinking time, shows the answer for a few seconds and moves to the next word.
The same tool works for science terms, maths vocabulary, foreign language words and general knowledge cards.

sections.heading: A notice board that is quick to change
paragraphs: Paper notices fade and pile up. A screen that rotates a few big messages is easy to read and easy to change: type a new heading, pick a colour and the next loop shows it.
Because each message fills the screen, it can be read from a distance. Colours help the important notice stand out from the greeting.

sections.heading: Greetings and announcements
paragraphs: Wish a colleague a happy birthday on the reception screen, welcome a visiting guest, announce a holiday closure, remind staff about a meeting or thank volunteers after an event. Add a photo or a logo where it helps.
Samples are included for a welcome board, birthday wishes and notices. Replace the text with your own.

sections.heading: For offices, schools and homes
paragraphs: Offices and shops use it for reception and break rooms. Schools use it at the entrance and in the staff room. Families use it on a TV for a birthday or an anniversary party.
Your messages and pictures are saved in your browser. If the browser is full, pictures may not be kept, so keep a copy of important ones.

sections.heading: Any routine, one step at a time
paragraphs: A routine is easier to follow when the screen shows the current step, how long is left and what comes next. This display does exactly that for any list of steps: a morning stretch, a desk break, a class station rotation, a recipe or a workshop procedure.
You can start from a ready routine or build your own in a minute: type the step names, write a cue if you like, set the seconds and add a picture where it helps.

sections.heading: Pictures from a free exercise list
paragraphs: Stretches and exercises can be added from a list of 182 entries, each with two pictures that fade into each other so people can see the movement. The list has 64 stretches, including neck, shoulder, back, hip, hamstring and calf stretches, chair stretches for a desk break and floor stretches for a cool-down.

The pictures come from the free-exercise-db project and are in the public domain. For anything not in the list, such as a yoga pose, a kitchen step or a lab setup, add a picture of your own or show the step without one.

sections.heading: Where it helps
paragraphs: Teachers use it for station rotations and brain breaks, yoga and fitness instructors for a class on a studio TV, offices for a five minute stretch break, parents for a kids’ morning routine, and cooks and workshops for timed steps.
This page gives general information and not medical advice. Warm up, move gently and stop if something hurts.
